object_audited: The Rigvedic corpus as a source for substrate vocabulary
who_created_the_surviving_record: A priestly lineage composing and transmitting liturgical poetry for patrons; the surviving text is what that lineage chose to preserve and what the canonisation fixed.
what_preserved_it: Oral transmission under a memorisation discipline, later writing, later still the printed editions of Aufrecht and Lubotsky and the Zurich annotation.
what_was_unlikely_to_be_recorded: Ordinary speech, non-liturgical genres, the vocabulary of people who were not patrons or priests, and any language spoken by anyone the hymns do not address. Agricultural, craft and domestic vocabulary enters only where the liturgy needed it.
what_is_unexcavated_or_unrecognised: Nothing to excavate. The relevant unrecognised category is vocabulary that IS in the text but is not recognised as foreign because it has been fully nativised.
absence_type: NOT PRODUCED for most of the lexicon of the region; NOT RECOGNISED for nativised loans.
effect_on_this_unit: The 0.013% figure (DE-M-011) is a floor on what a liturgical corpus recorded, not an estimate of contact. A corpus of this genre would under-record loan vocabulary even if contact were intense.

object_audited: CDIAL as the instrument of attribution
who_created_the_surviving_record: R. L. Turner, compiling in Britain 1962-66 from published sources and colonial-era descriptive material.
what_preserved_it: Print, then the DSAL digitization, then the JAMBU re-parse.
what_was_unlikely_to_be_recorded: Languages with no published dictionary in Turner's window; oral registers; anything the colonial descriptive tradition did not reach. The attribution can only be as good as the Dravidian and Munda lexicography available to him.
what_is_unexcavated_or_unrecognised: Munda lexicography was substantially thinner than Dravidian lexicography in that window.
absence_type: NOT PRODUCED (the comparanda did not exist to be consulted).
effect_on_this_unit: This is a live alternative explanation for DE-M-004's 4.1-to-1 ratio and it is not tested here: Turner may prefer Dravidian partly because he had far better Dravidian dictionaries. The ratio is registered as a fact about Turner (DE-I-004) precisely so this remains visible.

object_audited: The retrieval channel of this session
who_created_the_surviving_record: An egress policy set outside this programme.
what_preserved_it: GitHub, and only GitHub. The git proxy's anonymous lane (SRC-058) is the sole general channel.
what_was_unlikely_to_be_recorded: Anything that exists as a journal article, a monograph or a library digitization rather than as a public git repository. That is the entire secondary literature of the substrate question.
what_is_unexcavated_or_unrecognised: Witzel 1999, Kuiper 1991, Masica 1979, Krishnamurti 2003, Rau 2019, Shorto 2006 - none reachable.
effect_on_this_unit: Structural and asymmetric. Attested and reconstructed families have machine-readable derivatives on GitHub; proposals about unattested donors do not. Five distinctions could be measured and four could not, and the split follows the channel, not the evidence (DE-I-001, HOLD-005).

object_audited: DEDR as the record of attested Dravidian
who_created_the_surviving_record: Burrow and Emeneau, working 1961-84, drawing on missionary and colonial lexicography and on their own and Bhattacharya's fieldnotes.
what_preserved_it: Print; the DSAL digitization; the JAMBU re-parse. The chain's middle link is blocked to this session (DEP-010).
what_was_unlikely_to_be_recorded: Languages without a dictionary; speakers not consulted; the labour of the informants, which the entry numbers do not record.
what_is_unexcavated_or_unrecognised: The 77 language labels mix languages, dialects and unpublished fieldnote lects (EM-01), so the inventory reflects who did fieldwork where.
absence_type: NOT RECORDED (informant authorship); NOT ACCESSIBLE (the intermediate digitization).
effect_on_this_unit: EM-01's 77 is a count of Burrow and Emeneau's coverage, not of Dravidian. Constitution §4.V: preservation is not authorship. The fieldnote rows in this table were spoken by people the citation format does not name.

who_created_the_surviving_record: A shorter and more recent descriptive tradition than the Dravidian one, assembled here through Rau 2019 with per-language sources.
what_was_unlikely_to_be_recorded: The full lexicon of any Munda language. This is a wordlist built for reconstruction, not a dictionary.
what_is_unexcavated_or_unrecognised: Whether anything Munda-affiliated ever lay west of Korku - the question that decides HYP-E-002 - is exactly what no surviving record addresses.
absence_type: NOT PRODUCED / NOT RECOGNISED, undetermined between them.
effect_on_this_unit: The small size of the Munda evidence base in this record (DE-M-015) is partly a fact about lexicography and must not be read straight as a fact about the language family's history or extent.

who_created_the_surviving_record: E. V. Arnold, Cambridge 1905, working within the philological assumptions of his period.
what_preserved_it: Transcribed into strata.json by Gunkel and Ryan; distributed with VedaWeb.
what_was_unlikely_to_be_recorded: Any stratification criterion Arnold did not use.
what_is_unexcavated_or_unrecognised: Whether the metrical layering tracks composition date at all is an assumption inside the instrument, not a result from it.
absence_type: Not an absence question; a single-source question.
effect_on_this_unit: Every stratum claim in this unit is single-sourced (DEP-001) and the Popular stratum is not independent of book order (DEP-004). DE-I-006 and BR-E-002 are capped accordingly.

object_audited: The Rigvedic fort corpus as this repository can read it: 103 passages, four editions, nine translations, one dictionary
who_created_the_surviving_record: Brahmanical priestly lineages composed and transmitted the hymns; the surviving apparatus around them - the Aufrecht text, the padapāṭha edition, the lemmatisation, the gloss, and every translation this unit used - was made by European philologists between 1861 and 1951, and digitised by the VedaWeb project.
what_preserved_it: Oral transmission within priestly families, then European print scholarship, then a German-funded digital corpus. Each stage preserved what its makers valued and indexed it on their categories.
what_was_unlikely_to_be_recorded: Anything a hymn corpus does not praise. Construction technique for any structure (DJ-009). Who built a púr-, who was inside one when it was broken, what the people so described called themselves or their walls. The corpus names the breaker, not the built. Every count in this unit is a count of what Indra's poets said, and the losing side of every fort passage left no text.
what_is_unexcavated_or_unrecognised: Whether any excavated fortification corresponds to any passage. This unit retrieved NO archaeological source, no geography and no absolute chronology - the three things the identification question turns on - so the whole material record is unexamined here rather than examined and found silent.
absence_type: NOT PRODUCED for construction technique and for the defenders' account; NOT ACCESSIBLE for the archaeological and secondary literature, which exists and is EGRESS_BLOCKED (SRC-085, SRC-087)
effect_on_this_unit: Caps every lexical result in this unit at a statement about Grassmann's dictionary rather than about Rigvedic meaning (DEP-005, DEP-021, DEP-022). Makes HYP-J-001's verdict NOT-ELIGIBLE-SOURCE-BLOCKED rather than NOT-ELIGIBLE. Means DJ-I-02 must state the corpus gives no evidence EITHER way, which it now does.

object_audited: The reception of the Rigvedic forts in modern scholarship
who_created_the_surviving_record: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century European Indology built the fort passages into an invasion narrative; twentieth- and twenty-first-century Indian scholarship, including the chapter §4J's prohibition is written against, reads them onto the Indus archaeology; both readings are politically load-bearing in the present.
what_preserved_it: Commercial academic publishing. The single chapter that states this domain's named trap is paywalled behind a British commercial publisher and unreachable from here (SRC-086, SRC-087, D-046).
what_was_unlikely_to_be_recorded: Any reading of these passages made outside the European philological line and outside commercial anglophone publishing. Sāyaṇa - the pre-modern commentary that would sit outside it entirely - is not in the pinned corpus and was not retrieved.
what_is_unexcavated_or_unrecognised: The specialist standing of either reading. Step 11 could not be run: no citation record is reachable (api.crossref.org, api.openalex.org both blocked).
effect_on_this_unit: This unit gated a thesis it could not read, using a lexicon written by the tradition the thesis argues against. That asymmetry is recorded on every leg of HYP-J-001 and is the reason its verdict carries SOURCE-BLOCKED. It is NOT corrected by the gate; it is disclosed by it.
